citation: Bucol, A. A., & Catid, R. (2011). Fishes and Macroinvertebrates of Señora River, Siquijor Island, Philippines with New Records of the Genus Puntius (Cyprinidae) in the Visayas. Silliman Journal, 52(2), July–December 2011.

accessReview.publisherRecord: Article page and full 14-page publisher PDF reviewed. The PDF identifies Volume 52, Number 2, July–December 2011; the landing page also displays an October 2022 platform publication date and cites 2022. Use the issue and fieldwork dates, not that platform date, when describing the evidence.
accessReview.tableTranscription: Not performed. Table 1 is visible in parsed PDF text but is not copied into this review.
accessReview.reuse: The journal policy says copyright is held jointly by the journal and individual authors and specifies written permission for certain reproductions. No open data license or permission to extract/redistribute a structured species table was found. Seek written guidance before making a derivative checklist or public app data.

evidenceScope.waterbody: Señora River, Lazi, Siquijor; survey covered an upstream tributary, middle river reach, and estuarine reach.

stations.reach: middle channel near the main-channel/tributary junction

evidenceScope.collectionAndIdentification: The article reports gillnets, hook-and-line, fine-mesh nets and underwater camera observation. Samples were processed at Siquijor State College; some were deposited at the Silliman University Rodolfo B. Gonzales Museum of Natural History and gobioid specimens needing confirmation were deposited at the Smithsonian. The article reports specialist confirmation for several groups.
evidenceScope.reportedFishRichness: The abstract and Table 1 footer report 33 fish species, while the Results text reports 34. Do not silently resolve this discrepancy or use the count as a completeness denominator.
evidenceScope.ecologyAndHabitat: The study includes a named estuarine station and source-era ecological classes spanning freshwater, diadromous, euryhaline and marine visitors. It is not a purely freshwater inventory.
evidenceScope.taxonomy: No fish names transcribed into a structured research list. The article uses historical taxonomy; source strings and station marks need a separate visual/table review and modern specialist crosswalk.

decision.use: High-value historical primary-source lead for a specific Siquijor river; metadata and sampling design only at this stage.
decision.reason: The source has a 33-versus-34 fish-count conflict, combines river and estuary stations, provides coordinates without a datum, uses historical names, and has no verified structured-data reuse permission.

limitations: Field evidence is from 2011 and does not establish contemporary occupancy or current river condition.
The station coordinates are transcribed as DMS metadata only; no datum is stated and no map points are created.
The source has an unresolved fish-richness contradiction (33 in abstract/table; 34 in Results).
Three station counts or aggregate species totals are not a complete river inventory or current species coverage count.
The estuarine station requires separation from upstream freshwater evidence.
The downloadable publisher PDF is not itself proof of an open reuse license.
nextActions: Seek written guidance or permission from the journal and authors before extracting or publishing a structured Table 1 checklist.
If authorized, visually verify every Table 1 row and station mark, reconcile 33 versus 34 against the PDF, and preserve verbatim source names before taxonomy review.
Keep the estuary station separate from upstream freshwater evidence; do not infer the collection reach for any species without a visible station mark.
Continue Negros freshwater source review with the publisher-hosted Bago River fish study and Pagatban River sources; retain separate rights and historical-date holds.
